Its signature is FireAllClients(arguments: Tuple) and it returns nothing; the data is delivered to each client's OnClientEvent handler. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/remote-event.md

FireClient is a RemoteEvent method used by the server to send data to one specific client. Its signature is FireClient(player: Player, arguments: Tuple) and returns nothing. Note that in Vortex 0.3.4, the method is exposed but its delivery has not yet been confirmed. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/remote-event.md

FireServer is a RemoteEvent method called from the client to send data to the server. Its signature is FireServer(arguments: Tuple) and returns nothing. It triggers the server-side OnServerEvent handler and was confirmed working in Vortex Studio 0.3.4 for editor-authored remotes in ReplicatedStorage. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/remote-event.md

OnClientEvent is a RemoteEvent signal fired on the client when the server sends data via FireClient or FireAllClients. Its signature is OnClientEvent(arguments: Tuple): Signal. The event is exposed in Vortex 0.3.4, although delivery has not yet been fully established. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/remote-event.md

OnServerEvent is a RemoteEvent signal fired on the server when a client invokes FireServer. Its signature is OnServerEvent(senderId: Number, arguments: Tuple): Signal. In Vortex the senderId is a numeric connection identifier rather than a Player object, so it cannot currently be mapped back to a specific player, character, or humanoid. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/remote-event.md

RemoteFunction is a networking object in Vortex that, unlike RemoteEvent, lets data be computed inside a function call and the resulting values returned to the caller. It supports calling from server to client and from client to server, but does not support an InvokeAllClients because reliably yielding until every player has returned a value is not guaranteed. Instances of RemoteFunction are typically parented under ReplicatedStorage so both server and client scripts can access them. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/remote-function.md

InvokeClient is a method on RemoteFunction used by the server to invoke data from the server to a specific client. Its signature is InvokeClient(player: Player, arguments: Tuple) : Tuple, where player is the target Player and arguments is a tuple of values sent to the client, and it yields until the client returns a tuple response via OnClientInvoke. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/remote-function.md

InvokeServer is a method on RemoteFunction used by the client to invoke data from the client to the server. Its signature is InvokeServer(arguments: Tuple) : Tuple, where arguments is a tuple of values sent to the server, and it returns the tuple that the server produces via its OnServerInvoke callback. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/remote-function.md

OnClientInvoke is a writable callback on RemoteFunction that runs on the client in response to InvokeClient from the server. Its signature is OnClientInvoke(arguments: Tuple) : Tuple, where arguments is the tuple the server passed, and whatever tuple it returns is sent back to the server. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/remote-function.md

OnServerInvoke is a writable callback on RemoteFunction that runs on the server in response to InvokeServer from a client. Its signature is OnServerInvoke(senderId: Number, arguments: Tuple) : Tuple, where senderId is a numeric identifier for the invoking client and arguments is the tuple the client sent; the returned tuple is delivered back to that client. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/remote-function.md

questions: What are the Vortex Studio 0.3.4 RemoteFunction limitations?
Explain the Vortex Studio 0.3.4 RemoteFunction limitations
How do I handle the Vortex Studio 0.3.4 RemoteFunction limitations?
Tell me about the Vortex Studio 0.3.4 RemoteFunction limitations
answer: In Vortex Studio 0.3.4, InvokeServer is exposed on the client and OnServerInvoke can be assigned in a Script for an editor-authored RemoteFunction under ReplicatedStorage. However, InvokeServer(LocalPlayer) is rejected before delivery because Instances cannot currently be sent through remotes, so a successful primitive request/response round trip has not yet been established. The server-side Players:GetChildren() route is unavailable, but Players:GetPlayers() does return visible Player objects in a server Script, providing the Player target in principle. OnClientInvoke and InvokeClient delivery are still untested in this version. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/remote-function.md

ReplicatedStorage is a service container whose contents are loaded by both the server and the client. Instances placed inside it automatically have their properties synced from the server to clients. It is accessed via game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"). Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/replicated-storage.md

ClassName is a String property of ReplicatedStorage that holds the runtime class name of the service. It is read-only and identifies the service type during execution. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/replicated-storage.md

Name is a String property of ReplicatedStorage that stores the service name shown by the runtime. It identifies the service within the game's hierarchy. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/replicated-storage.md

FindFirstChild is a method on ReplicatedStorage with the signature ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild(name: String). It returns the first direct child matching the supplied name, or nil if no such child exists. Only direct (non-recursive) children are searched. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/replicated-storage.md

GetChildren is a method on ReplicatedStorage that returns an array of Instance values representing the direct children of the service. It provides a snapshot of the immediate contents rather than a recursive listing. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/replicated-storage.md

WaitForChild is a method on ReplicatedStorage with the signature ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild(name: String). It blocks until a direct child with the supplied name appears and then returns that Instance. It is useful for synchronizing code that depends on a replicated instance that may not exist yet at runtime. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/replicated-storage.md

questions: What is Parenting instances to ReplicatedStorage?
Explain Parenting instances to ReplicatedStorage in Vortex
How do I use Parenting instances to ReplicatedStorage?
Tell me about Parenting instances to ReplicatedStorage
answer: To place an instance into ReplicatedStorage, the developer creates it with Instance.new and sets its Parent property to the ReplicatedStorage service. For example, a new Part can be named "SharedPart" and assigned as a child of ReplicatedStorage so that both server and client can see it. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/replicated-storage.md

questions: What is Vortex Studio 0.3.4 testing notes?
Explain Vortex Studio 0.3.4 testing notes in Vortex
How do I use Vortex Studio 0.3.4 testing notes?
Tell me about Vortex Studio 0.3.4 testing notes
answer: These notes document observed behavior in Vortex Studio version 0.3.4 and may not apply to later releases. They confirm that a temporary Part can be parented to ReplicatedStorage and that WaitForChild will resolve it, while FindFirstChild returns nil and GetChildren omits it under the same conditions. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/replicated-storage.md

ServerScriptService is a Roblox-style service obtained via game:GetService("ServerScriptService") in Vortex Studio 0.3.4. It is accessible from both Script and LocalScript execution contexts and provides standard enumeration methods such as FindFirstChild, GetChildren, and WaitForChild. A notable limitation is that Scripts created at runtime do not appear as observable children of this service: parent-equality checks and FindFirstChild will not locate them, and GetChildren() will exclude them. To work reliably, server Scripts should be authored and placed in the editor rather than instantiated programmatically. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/server-script-service.md

SpawnLocation is a specialized Part used to define where player characters load into the world. It inherits from the base part class. Its primary purpose is providing a spawn point for players when they join or respawn. SpawnLocation inherits all standard Part properties such as Color, Transparency, Material, Cast Shadow, Anchored, CanCollide, Truss, Name, Position, Rotation, and Size. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/spawnlocation.md

questions: Explain SpawnLocation runtime availability in Vortex
How do I use SpawnLocation runtime availability?
Tell me about SpawnLocation runtime availability
answer: In Vortex Studio 0.3.4, calling Instance.new("SpawnLocation") fails in both Script and LocalScript contexts. A workspace descendant scan also did not find any live SpawnLocation instances in the tested project. This means the editor-facing property documentation is not confirmed to be a working runtime scripting surface in this version. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/spawnlocation.md

A SpotLight in Vortex is a conical light that emits from a single point in 3D space. It must be parented to a Part, and it inherits its position from the parent Part. There is no built-in on/off switch, but setting the Color, Brightness, Angle, or Range to 0 will visually disable the light. Under the Properties tab, SpotLight displays Position, Rotation, and Size attributes, but Position and Rotation are read-only while Size has no effect. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/spot-light.md

questions: What is the SpotLight runtime scripting limitation?
Explain the SpotLight runtime scripting limitation in Vortex
How do I use the SpotLight runtime scripting limitation?
Tell me about the SpotLight runtime scripting limitation
answer: In Vortex Studio 0.3.4, calling Instance.new("SpotLight") succeeds in both Script and LocalScript but returns a non-functional shell. The instance only exposes generic Instance methods plus a connectable Changed signal, while the tested light-specific fields initially read as nil. Brightness, Range, Angle, Enabled, and Shadows cannot be set, and although Color accepts and retains a Color3 value, assigning Parent to a temporary Part does not actually establish parentage. As a result, there is no confirmed script route for configuring or attaching a rendered SpotLight in the current runtime. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/spot-light.md

Angle is a Float property of a SpotLight that defines the spread of the emission cone. Smaller values produce a sharper, more focused cutoff, while wider values create a softer fall-off at the edges of the cone. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/spot-light.md

Brightness is a Float property of a SpotLight that controls how intensely the light is emitted. It affects only the strength of the light and does not influence how far the light reaches. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/spot-light.md

Color is a Color3 property of a SpotLight that determines the color tint of the emitted light. Darker colors effectively behave like turning the light off. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/spot-light.md

Face is an Enum.Face property of a SpotLight that selects which face of the parent Part the light is emitted from. By choosing a different face, the direction of the cone can be aimed along a specific axis of the parent. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/spot-light.md

Name is a String property of a SpotLight that serves as both the internal identifier and the label shown in the Explorer panel. Changing it renames the instance in the hierarchy. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/spot-light.md

Range is a Float property of a SpotLight that specifies the maximum linear distance the light can reach. It governs how the brightness falls off over distance, but increasing it does not make the light itself brighter. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/spot-light.md

StarterPlayerScripts is a container located inside the StarterPlayer service that holds client-side scripts. When a player joins the experience, the contents of StarterPlayerScripts are automatically copied into that player's PlayerScripts container. It is designed primarily for LocalScripts, which execute on the client side of the experience. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/starter-player-scripts.md

PlayerScripts is the per-player destination container where scripts from StarterPlayerScripts are copied when a player joins the experience. It serves as the runtime location for client-side scripts associated with that specific player during their session. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/starter-player-scripts.md

StarterPlayerScripts is commonly used for client-side game systems, player input handling, camera systems, client-side effects and animations, user interface logic, keyboard, mouse, and controller input, local player movement systems, and client-side visual effects. It houses code that runs on the player's device for player-specific behavior. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/starter-player-scripts.md

questions: Explain the StarterCharacterScripts distinction in Vortex
How do I use the StarterCharacterScripts distinction?
Tell me about the StarterCharacterScripts distinction
answer: StarterCharacterScripts should not be confused with StarterPlayerScripts. Although both look similar, they have different purposes: StarterPlayerScripts focuses on client-side player systems, while StarterCharacterScripts is intended for scripts tied to the player's character specifically. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/starter-player-scripts.md

questions: What script types run in StarterPlayerScripts?
Explain script types in StarterPlayerScripts in Vortex
How do I use script types in StarterPlayerScripts?
Tell me about script types in StarterPlayerScripts
answer: StarterPlayerScripts is primarily intended for LocalScripts, which run on the client. Server Scripts placed there will not run on the server. ModuleScripts can be placed inside StarterPlayerScripts when they will be required by other client-side scripts, but for modules that need to be shared by both client and server, ReplicatedStorage is the recommended location. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/starter-player-scripts.md

questions: What are the StarterPlayerScripts security considerations?
How do I use StarterPlayerScripts security considerations?
answer: StarterPlayerScripts should never be used for server-side security or validation, since the client is controlled by the player and cannot be trusted. Server validation, anti-cheat enforcement, and other security-critical logic must always run on the server rather than in client-side scripts placed in StarterPlayerScripts. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/starter-player-scripts.md

StringValue is a container object in Vortex Studio 0.3.4 that stores a single string field called Value. Unlike typical Roblox-style ValueBase descendants, it is detached and does not need a parent to be read from or written to. It can be instantiated from both Script and LocalScript contexts using Instance.new("StringValue"). Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/string-value.md

Value is the string property of a StringValue instance. A newly created StringValue starts with the empty string as its Value, and scripts can assign and read it directly, for example: message.Value = "Hello, Vortex" followed by print(message.Value) prints the assigned text. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/string-value.md

Name is the standard string instance name property of StringValue. By default, a freshly constructed StringValue has its Name set to the string "StringValue". Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/string-value.md

Changed is the signal on StringValue that can be connected to a callback function. In the tested 0.3.4 runtime, however, mutating the Value property did not actually fire this callback, so scripts that need to observe updates should poll Value instead of relying on Changed. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/string-value.md

GetPropertyChangedSignal is a method on StringValue that returns a signal for a specified property, used as GetPropertyChangedSignal("Value") to listen for Value changes. As of the tested 0.3.4 build, the returned signal is connectable but does not fire when Value is modified, so polling Value is recommended for reliable change detection. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/string-value.md

A Texture in Vortex is an editor-facing concept used to render special decals onto a Part. When added through the editor, its Face and name are assigned automatically, allowing six textures to cover all faces of a part efficiently. Texture scripting is not currently exposed in the Vortex runtime; only two texture choices are available, and there is no confirmed script API for creating or modifying textures. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/texture.md

Face is a property of Texture that determines which side of the parent Part the texture appears on. It is typed as Enum.Face, matching the standard face enum used elsewhere in Vortex. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/texture.md

Texture is a property of Texture that selects which decal image gets rendered on the chosen face. It is typed as Enum.Texture, and at the time of writing the only available options are Inlets and Studs. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/texture.md

questions: Explain Texture scripting support in Vortex
How do I use Texture scripting support?
Tell me about Texture scripting support
answer: In Vortex Studio 0.3.4, calls such as Instance.new("Texture"), Instance.new("Decal"), and Instance.new("SurfaceAppearance") fail in both Script and LocalScript contexts. Script-created Parts also lack readable Texture, TextureID, SurfaceAppearance, or Decal fields, so there is currently no confirmed script API for creating or changing textures even though editor-authored textures are supported. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/texture.md

UserInputService is a service that receives keyboard and other player input on the client side in Vortex. It is accessed via `game:GetService("UserInputService")` inside a `LocalScript`, since it is not usable from a regular server Script. The service exposes input-related events such as InputBegan and InputEnded. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/user-input-service.md

InputBegan is a signal on UserInputService that fires when input begins. Its callback receives an InputObject whose KeyCode can be compared with an Enum.KeyCode value to detect specific keys. It can also be used with `:Once` and `:Wait` in a LocalScript, both of which delivered a right-mouse-button input in testing. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/user-input-service.md

InputEnded is a signal on UserInputService that fires when input ends. In testing on Vortex Studio 0.3.4 it was connectable in a LocalScript and delivered both keyboard and mouse-button release events. It is exposed as a standard signal that can be connected with `:Connect`. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/user-input-service.md

IsKeyDown is a UserInputService method used to check whether a given key is currently being pressed. In Vortex Studio 0.3.4 testing, it returned `true` for the keyboard key currently pressed and `false` for mouse-button events. It is available on the service. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/user-input-service.md

InputChanged is a UserInputService event related to changes in input state. In Vortex Studio 0.3.4, it read as `nil` and could not be connected. It therefore is not currently usable in that client version. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/user-input-service.md

GetMouseLocation is a UserInputService method intended to return the mouse's current screen position. As of Vortex Studio 0.3.4, it was unavailable on the tested client and could not be used. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/user-input-service.md

MouseBehavior is a UserInputService property that controls how the mouse behaves in the client. In Vortex Studio 0.3.4 testing it read as `nil`, meaning it was not yet implemented in that build. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/user-input-service.md

MouseIconEnabled is a UserInputService property that toggles the visibility of the mouse cursor icon. In the tested Vortex Studio 0.3.4 client it read as `nil`, indicating it was not available in that version. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/user-input-service.md

KeyboardEnabled is a UserInputService boolean property indicating whether keyboard input is available. The Vortex Studio 0.3.4 client reported `KeyboardEnabled=true`. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/user-input-service.md

MouseEnabled is a UserInputService boolean property indicating whether mouse input is available. The Vortex Studio 0.3.4 client reported `MouseEnabled=true`. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/user-input-service.md

GamepadEnabled is a UserInputService boolean property indicating whether gamepad input is supported. The Vortex Studio 0.3.4 client reported `GamepadEnabled=false`. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/user-input-service.md

TouchEnabled is a UserInputService boolean property indicating whether touch input is supported. The Vortex Studio 0.3.4 client reported `TouchEnabled=false`. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/user-input-service.md

InputObject is the data type passed to UserInputService input event callbacks. It carries a KeyCode that can be compared against Enum.KeyCode values for keyboard input, while mouse-button events used `Enum.KeyCode.Unknown` in testing. It also exposes a `gameProcessed` field, with both `false` and `true` values observed in Vortex Studio 0.3.4. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/user-input-service.md

Workspace is a service in Vortex that holds and renders every 3D player-interactable instance. It exposes the ClassName and Name string properties, along with methods for locating its child Instances such as FindFirstChild, GetChildren, and WaitForChild. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/workspace.md

ClassName is a String property of the Workspace service that represents its runtime class name. It reflects the class identity assigned by the Vortex runtime rather than the authored display Name. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/workspace.md

Name is a String property of the Workspace service that holds the service name as shown by the runtime. It is the identifier used when looking up Workspace via hierarchy calls. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/workspace.md

FindFirstChild is a Workspace method invoked as workspace:FindFirstChild(name: String) that returns the first direct child Instance with the matching name, or nil if no such child exists. Only direct children are searched, not deeper descendants. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/workspace.md

GetChildren is a Workspace method that returns a table containing the direct child Instances of Workspace. The note warns that repeated calls may yield fresh Lua wrapper tables for the same underlying Instance, so returned wrappers should not be used as persistent table keys across frames. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/workspace.md

WaitForChild is a Workspace method invoked as workspace:WaitForChild(name: String) that blocks until a direct child with the supplied name appears, then returns that Instance. It is useful for synchronizing code with Instances that are parented later in the lifecycle. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/workspace.md

CFrame.lookAt is a static constructor on the CFrame type that builds a new CFrame located at a specified position and rotated so that its forward axis points toward a target position. It accepts two Vector3 arguments: Position, which defines where the CFrame is placed, and LookAt, which is the world-space point the CFrame should face. It returns the resulting CFrame instance. Typical usage is for orienting parts or cameras so they look at another point in the world without manually computing rotation angles. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/cframe.lookat.md

Color3.fromRGB is a static constructor function on the Color3 type in Vortex that builds a new Color3 value from explicit red, green, and blue numeric components. Its signature is Color3.fromRGB(R: Number, G: Number, B: Number), taking three Number arguments where each channel is specified on the familiar 0 to 255 byte range. It returns a new Color3 instance representing the combined RGB color, which is the standard way to author colors from concrete 0-255 values. A typical use is Color3.fromRGB(255, 0, 0) to produce a fully saturated red Color3. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/color3.fromrgb.md

Color3 is a value type in Vortex that represents a color using three numeric components: a red, green, and blue channel. It exposes the properties R, G, and B (all of type Number), and supports constructors and a Lerp method for blending colors. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/color3.md

R is a Number property of a Color3 that stores the red component of the color. The value's expected range depends on which constructor created the Color3 (0 to 1 from new, 0 to 255 from fromRGB). Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/color3.md

G is a Number property of a Color3 that stores the green component of the color. Like R, its effective range is 0 to 1 for normalized Color3 values, or 0 to 255 for those produced via fromRGB. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/color3.md

B is a Number property of a Color3 that stores the blue component of the color. Its expected numeric range is determined by the constructor used (normalized 0-1 or byte 0-255). Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/color3.md

Color3.new is a constructor that takes three Number arguments (R, G, B) and returns a new Color3. The component values are expected to be in the normalized range of 0 to 1. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/color3.md

Color3.fromRGB is a constructor that takes three Number arguments (R, G, B) and returns a new Color3. Unlike Color3.new, the input values are expected to be in the 0 to 255 range, matching typical 8-bit-per-channel RGB color encoding. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/color3.md

Color3:Lerp is an instance method with the signature color:Lerp(other: Color3, alpha: Number) that returns a new Color3 computed as a component-wise linear interpolation between the calling color and the other Color3. The alpha parameter controls how far along the blend to go, with 0 returning the original color and 1 returning the target color. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/color3.md

In Vortex, a Connection is a value returned by Signal:Connect or Signal:Once that represents a link between a callback function and a Signal. It exists so the caller can later manage that link, for example to stop the callback from firing when the signal does. Internally it is implemented as a Luau table. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/connection.md

Connected is a Boolean property on a Connection that indicates whether the link is currently active. It starts as true when the Connection is first created and is set to false after Disconnect is called, meaning the callback will no longer receive signal fires. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/connection.md

Connection:Disconnect is a method invoked as connection:Disconnect() that severs the link between a callback and its Signal. Once called, subsequent signal fires will not invoke the callback and the Connection's Connected property becomes false. A lowercase disconnect alias is also available and behaves identically. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/connection.md

In Vortex, an Enum is a data type that represents a set of named constant values. Each enum exposes its individual options as EnumItem values and provides methods for looking them up by name, by numeric value, or for retrieving the full list of options at once. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/enum.md

GetEnumItems is a method on the Enum type that takes no arguments and returns an array of all EnumItem options that belong to that enum. The return type is EnumItem[], allowing callers to iterate over every defined option in the enum. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/enum.md

FromName is a method on the Enum type that accepts a single String argument named name and returns the matching EnumItem whose name equals the supplied string. It is used to look up a specific enum option by its textual identifier. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/enum.md

FromValue is a method on the Enum type that accepts a single Number argument named value and returns the EnumItem whose underlying numeric value matches. It provides an alternative lookup path when working with the integer representation of an enum option. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/enum.md

EnumItem represents a single entry within an enum in the Vortex platform. Each item is identified by a name and assigned an integral numeric value, and it keeps a reference back to the parent enum it belongs to. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/enumitem.md

Name is a String property of an EnumItem that holds the textual label of that enum entry. It is the human-readable identifier used to refer to the item. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/enumitem.md

Value is a Number property of an EnumItem representing the integral numeric value associated with the entry. This underlying integer distinguishes the item from others in the same enum. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/enumitem.md

EnumType is an Enum property of an EnumItem that points back to the parent enum containing this item. It allows code to traverse from an individual entry up to its owning enum. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/enumitem.md

InputObject is a Vortex data type that describes a single user input event. It lets the developer identify which input device produced the event, such as a keyboard key press, a mouse action, or another supported device, and to read state information, position, and other relevant details about that event. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/input-object.md

Debris is a cleanup service in Vortex used to schedule automatic removal of instances after a delay. It is accessible from both Scripts and LocalScripts via game:GetService("Debris"). The service provides AddItem for scheduling cleanup of a specific instance and SetMaxItems for configuring how many items it manages. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/debris.md

Debris:AddItem schedules an instance to be destroyed after a given lifetime. In Vortex Studio 0.3.4, calling Debris:AddItem(instance, 0) on an unparented temporary Part removed the instance within two scheduler ticks. It accepts the target instance and a lifetime value in seconds. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/debris.md

Debris:SetMaxItems is a method on the Debris service that configures the maximum number of items the service will track. It is exposed alongside AddItem on the Debris service in Vortex. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/debris.md

Enum is a runtime namespace in Vortex that organizes categorical constants into groups accessible via dot notation like `Enum.<group>.<item>`. Vortex Studio 0.3.4 revalidated the full member inventory across both Script and LocalScript contexts, confirming 119 items stable across reads and converting to their documented string form. The namespace covers groups such as EasingDirection, EasingStyle, KeyCode, Material, NormalId, PlaybackState, and UserInputType. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/enum.md

EasingDirection is an enum group under Enum that describes the direction of an easing curve. It contains three members: `In`, `InOut`, and `Out`, corresponding to the start, both ends, and end acceleration/deceleration patterns of tween animations. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/enum.md

EasingStyle is an enum group under Enum that selects the mathematical curve shape used for interpolation. Its members are `Back`, `Bounce`, `Circular`, `Cubic`, `Elastic`, `Exponential`, `Linear`, `Quad`, `Quart`, `Quint`, and `Sine`, each producing a distinct animation feel. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/enum.md

KeyCode is an enum group under Enum representing keyboard keys and a sentinel for unknown input. It includes letter keys A through Z, digits Zero through Nine, function keys F1 through F12, navigation keys Up/Down/Left/Right, modifier keys LeftAlt/LeftControl/LeftShift/LeftSuper and their Right counterparts, and punctuation/control keys such as BackSlash, Backquote, Backspace, Comma, Equals, Escape, LeftBracket, Minus, Period, Quote, Return, RightBracket, Semicolon, Slash, Space, Tab, and Delete. The `Unknown` member acts as a fallback when a key cannot be identified. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/enum.md

Material is an enum group under Enum describing the physical surface type of a part. It contains five members: `Grass`, `Ice`, `Metal`, `Plastic`, and `Wood`, each representing a different appearance and friction/collision behavior. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/enum.md

NormalId is an enum group under Enum identifying the six face directions of a part. Its members are `Back`, `Bottom`, `Front`, `Left`, `Right`, and `Top`, commonly used when working with surfaces, decals, and face-dependent operations. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/enum.md

PlaybackState is an enum group under Enum reporting the lifecycle phase of an animation or tween. Its members are `Begin`, `Cancelled`, `Completed`, `Delayed`, `Paused`, and `Playing`, allowing scripts to react to state transitions during playback. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/enum.md

UserInputType is an enum group under Enum categorizing the source of user input. Its members are `Focus`, `Gamepad1`, `Keyboard`, `MouseButton1`, `MouseButton2`, `MouseButton3`, `MouseMovement`, `MouseWheel`, `None`, and `Touch`, used in input event handling to distinguish input devices and modalities. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/enum.md

FromName is a method on each enum group that performs a name-based lookup. Its signature is `enumType:FromName(name: String)` and it returns the matching `EnumItem`, or `nil` if no item with that name exists in the group. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/enum.md

FromValue is a method on each enum group that performs a numeric lookup. Its signature is `enumType:FromValue(value: Number)` and it returns the `EnumItem` whose integral value matches the supplied number. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/enum.md

GetEnumItems is a method on each enum group that enumerates its members. Its signature is `enumType:GetEnumItems()` and it returns a table containing every `EnumItem` defined in that group, useful for iteration and inspection. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/enum.md

In Vortex, `game` is the root instance of a game and acts as the entry point for accessing services and other top-level objects. It exposes properties like `Workspace` and `Players` as direct children, a `GetService` method for retrieving services by name, and an optional `OnClose` callback. Several standard Roblox-style services such as ReplicatedStorage, ServerScriptService, Lighting, Debris, RunService, TweenService, and UserInputService are documented as children of `game`, though availability may vary between versions. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/game.md

questions: How do I use Workspace (game property)?
answer: `game.Workspace` is a property of the root `game` instance that returns the root `Workspace` service. It holds any object that exists in the 3D world and is also accessible via `game:GetService("Workspace")`. In testing on Vortex Studio 0.3.4, both access paths report `ClassName` and `Name` as `Workspace`. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/game.md

questions: How do I use Players (game property)?
answer: `game.Players` is a property of the root `game` instance that aliases the Players service, which tracks currently connected players. As of Vortex Studio 0.3.4 it is documented as a distinct proxy table from `game:GetService("Players")`. The service itself is the same one listed under `game`'s services. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/game.md

`game:GetService(serviceName: String)` is a method on the root game instance that returns the service matching the provided name as an `Instance`. The single parameter `serviceName` is a string identifying the service to retrieve. In Vortex Studio 0.3.4, `Lighting` cannot be obtained this way in either Script or LocalScript contexts. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/game.md

`game.OnClose` is an optional callback property on the root game instance that can be assigned a function to run before the game shuts down. Its type is `Function` or `nil`, and it begins as `nil` by default. As of Vortex Studio 0.3.4, assigning a function succeeds, but whether the callback is actually invoked on shutdown had not been verified. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/game.md

questions: How do I use ReplicatedStorage (game service)?
answer: ReplicatedStorage is a service listed under `game` that serves as a container for instances shared between the server and the client. It is returned as an `Instance` and is typically where assets and replicated objects are placed so both sides of the network can access them. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/game.md

questions: How do I use StarterPlayerScripts (game service)?
answer: StarterPlayerScripts is listed as a service under `game`, but the page marks it as a stub, indicating documentation is not yet complete. It is intended to be returned as an `Instance` and traditionally holds scripts that are cloned into each player's PlayerScripts when they join. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/game.md

questions: How do I use ServerScriptService (game service)?
answer: ServerScriptService is a service under `game` that holds `Script` instances which run when the server starts. It is returned as an `Instance` and is the standard location for server-side Lua code that should execute on game launch. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/game.md

questions: How do I use Lighting (game service)?
answer: Lighting is documented as a service under `game` that handles editor-facing lighting settings. As of Vortex Studio 0.3.4, however, `game:GetService("Lighting")` rejects the request in both Script and LocalScript contexts, meaning it is not exposed through `GetService` at runtime in that version. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/game.md

questions: How do I use Debris (game service)?
answer: Debris is one of the services listed under `game` in Vortex. It is returned as an `Instance` when requested and is conventionally used to schedule delayed cleanup of objects that are no longer needed in the world. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/game.md

questions: How do I use RunService (game service)?
answer: RunService is a service under `game` that exposes information about the runtime loop, such as frame and step callbacks. It is returned as an `Instance` and is typically used to bind to per-frame or per-step events on the client or server. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/game.md

questions: How do I use TweenService (game service)?
answer: TweenService is a service under `game` that is used to create and play tween animations on numeric properties of instances. It is returned as an `Instance` when requested via `game:GetService`. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/game.md

questions: How do I use UserInputService (game service)?
answer: UserInputService is a service under `game` that handles client-side input such as keyboard, mouse, touch, and gamepad events. It is returned as an `Instance` and is typically accessed from LocalScripts to respond to player input. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/game.md

Instance.new is a constructor function that creates a new Instance of a specified class in Vortex. It accepts a required className string identifying which class to instantiate, and an optional parent Instance to assign immediately. The constructor returns the freshly created Instance, which can then have its properties configured before parenting. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/instance-new.md

questions: Explain Instance.new parent argument in Vortex
How do I use Instance.new parent argument?
Tell me about Instance.new parent argument
answer: The parent parameter on Instance.new is an optional second argument that sets the Parent of the new instance at creation time. It accepts an Instance or nil. When omitted, the new instance begins unparented, and you must assign its Parent property separately after configuring it. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/instance-new.md

questions: Explain parenting new instances in Vortex
How do I use parenting new instances?
Tell me about parenting new instances
answer: A newly created Instance starts with no parent, so you should set its properties such as Name, Size, Position, and Anchored first. The Parent should be assigned last so that any scripts listening for the object observe it in a fully configured state. This ordering avoids partially initialized instances triggering downstream logic. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/instance-new.md

questions: Explain default Part state in Vortex
How do I use default Part state?
Tell me about default Part state
answer: In Vortex Studio 0.3.4, a freshly constructed Part is anchored, collidable, and casts shadows. Its Name is "Part", Position and rotation are both (0, 0, 0), CFrame is identity, Size is (4, 1, 2), Transparency is 0, and Color is approximately (0.64, 0.64, 0.64). Any property you do not explicitly assign retains its runtime default value. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/instance-new.md

Instance.fromExisting would be an API for cloning an existing Instance, but it is not exposed in Vortex Studio 0.3.4. Both Script and LocalScript contexts resolve it to nil in that release, so it cannot be used to duplicate instances. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/instance-new.md

questions: How do I use creatable classes?
answer: In Vortex Studio 0.3.4, common classes that can be instantiated through Instance.new include Part, Model, Folder, Script, LocalScript, ModuleScript, IntValue, StringValue, BindableEvent, RemoteEvent, RemoteFunction, PointLight, and SpotLight. By contrast, SpawnLocation, Texture, Decal, and SurfaceAppearance are not constructible in the tested runtime. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/instance-new.md

questions: What is GetChildren and FindFirstChild reliability?
Explain GetChildren and FindFirstChild reliability in Vortex
How do I use GetChildren and FindFirstChild reliability?
Tell me about GetChildren and FindFirstChild reliability
answer: In Vortex Studio 0.3.4, assigning Parent to a script-created instance, or passing the parent argument to Instance.new, is accepted by the runtime, but the children are not reliably listed by GetChildren or FindFirstChild on the parent service. You should not depend on these enumeration methods to expose runtime objects inside the editor-authored Workspace hierarchy in this release. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/instance-new.md

How do I use the coroutine library?
Tell me about the coroutine library
answer: The coroutine library in Vortex includes close, create, isyieldable, resume, running, status, wrap, and yield. close on a suspended coroutine returns true and leaves it dead, create returns a thread, a fresh coroutine reports suspended, resume returns multiple values starting with a success boolean, and running returns the current thread along with a nil main-thread flag. questions: Explain the string library in Vortex
How do I use the string library?

answer: Vortex's string library includes byte, char, find, format, gmatch, gsub, len, lower, match, pack, packsize, rep, reverse, split, sub, unpack, and upper. Notable features include format accepting %s and %d placeholders, pack supporting format strings like "<I2" with packsize reporting the byte length, split returning a count plus the resulting substrings, and unpack returning the decoded value plus the position after it. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/legacy.md

questions: Explain the table library in Vortex

Notable behaviors include clone producing a shallow copy whose mutations don't affect the original, freeze making tables immutable and verifiable via isfrozen, maxn returning the largest numeric key, and move copying elements into a destination table at a given offset. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/legacy.md

In addition, math.isfinite, math.isinf, math.isnan, task.cancel, task.desynchronize, and task.synchronize are not available and resolve to nil as well. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/legacy.md

The `print` function is available in both Script and LocalScript in Vortex Studio 0.3.4. It accepts multiple arguments and formats Vortex-specific values like `Vector3` for display in the Output panel, and it always returns `nil`. While the game is running, output is labelled with the type of script that produced it, so adding your own prefixes is recommended when multiple scripts emit related diagnostics. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/output.md

The `warn` function is unavailable in Vortex Studio. It cannot be used for emitting warning-level diagnostics, so alternative approaches such as prefixed `print` statements must be used instead. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/output.md

The `error` function is available in Vortex Studio and raises a runtime error with a given message. When called inside a `pcall`, it causes the `pcall` to return `false` along with a string that includes the generated script identifier, the line number where `error` was invoked, and the supplied message. An uncaught call to `error` ends the current script path and should be used deliberately when debugging. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/output.md

The `assert` function is available in Vortex Studio and behaves similarly to standard Luau, raising an error when its condition is falsy. When used inside a `pcall`, a failed assertion causes the protected call to return `false` together with an error string containing the script identifier, line number, and the assertion's message. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/output.md

questions: Explain the Output panel in Vortex
How do I use the Output panel?
Tell me about the Output panel
answer: The Output panel is the Vortex Studio surface where script diagnostics produced by `print` are displayed, with automatic formatting for Vortex values such as `Vector3`. Each line of output is labelled with the type of the script that produced it while the game is running, which helps trace diagnostics back to their source when multiple scripts are active. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/output.md

RunService is a Vortex service accessed via game:GetService("RunService") that exposes runtime context helpers and a per-frame heartbeat signal. It provides methods IsClient, IsServer, and IsStudio for detecting the execution environment, and exposes a Heartbeat signal that fires every runtime update with a deltaTime parameter in seconds. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/runservice.md

IsClient is a method on RunService that takes no arguments and returns a Boolean. It indicates whether the current script is executing in a client context, returning true inside a LocalScript and false inside a Script. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/runservice.md

IsServer is a method on RunService that takes no arguments and returns a Boolean. It indicates whether the current script is executing in a server context, returning true inside a Script and false inside a LocalScript, behaving as the inverse of IsClient. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/runservice.md

IsStudio is a method on RunService that takes no arguments and returns a Boolean. It indicates whether the current runtime is Vortex Studio rather than a live client or server, and testing in version 0.3.4 showed it returning true in both client and server contexts. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/runservice.md

Heartbeat is a Signal on RunService that fires once per runtime update. It passes a single parameter called deltaTime, a Number representing the elapsed time in seconds since the previous update, and the signal supports Connect, Once, and Wait methods. Because deltaTime varies between updates, it should not be treated as a fixed interval. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/runservice.md

task.defer is a runtime scheduling helper that queues a callback to run during a later scheduler cycle without yielding the thread that called it. Its signature is task.defer(callback: Function, ...: any), where the callback is the function to schedule and any extra arguments are forwarded to it. In Vortex Studio 0.3.4, a deferred callback is still pending after one task.wait() call and finishes during the second wait cycle. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/task.md

task.delay schedules a callback to be executed after a specified number of seconds, again without yielding the caller. Its signature is task.delay(duration: Number, callback: Function, ...: any), where duration is measured in seconds and additional arguments are passed through to the callback. Behavior in Vortex Studio 0.3.4 mirrors task.defer, remaining pending through one task.wait() cycle and completing on the next. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/task.md

task.spawn runs a callback as soon as the scheduler can without pausing the thread that invoked it. Its signature is task.spawn(callback: Function, ...: any), with optional varargs forwarded into the callback. Unlike defer or delay, in Vortex Studio 0.3.4 task.spawn finishes executing during the scheduling call itself rather than waiting for a later cycle. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/task.md

task.wait suspends the current thread until the scheduler resumes it, or until an optional duration has elapsed. Its signature is task.wait(duration: Number?): Number, where the optional argument is a wait time in seconds and the return value is the elapsed time as a number. It is the main way to yield execution in Vortex's task module. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/task.md

TweenInfo is a global constructor in Vortex used to configure the animation parameters of a Tween, such as duration and easing behavior. An instance is created with TweenInfo.new, passing arguments that define properties like time, easing style, easing direction, repeat count, reverses flag, and delay. Setting the repeatCount argument to -1 causes the tween to repeat forever, and a separate datatype reference page provides the complete parameter details. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/tween-info.md

Instances are the fundamental building blocks for objects in a Vortex game, where each concrete class comes with its own Properties and methods. A new Instance can be created in a script by calling Instance.new and passing the desired ClassName as the first argument. Vortex does not currently expose a universal base API on every engine-backed value, so common hierarchy methods may be available on classes like Part but not on Player or Humanoid. Developers should consult the concrete class reference, which contains the tested Vortex Studio 0.3.4 availability matrix, before calling a particular method. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/guides/instances.md

Instance.new is a global method used in scripts to create a new Instance in Vortex. It takes the ClassName of the desired Instance as its first argument and returns a new object of that class. This is the primary way to programmatically spawn new engine-backed objects at runtime. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/guides/instances.md

Instance is a shared convention used in Vortex for engine-backed objects, similar to Roblox's Instance. Vortex Studio 0.3.4 does not expose one uniform Instance method set on every engine-backed value, so the members listed describe ordinary Instance-like objects rather than a guaranteed interface. Each Instance-like object shares common properties (Name, Parent) and common methods (Clone, Destroy, GetChildren), but actual method availability depends on the concrete class. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/instance.md

Instance.Name is a String property that holds the name assigned to an Instance-like object. It is one of the two common properties shared across engine-backed values in Vortex. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/instance.md

Instance.Parent is a property of type `Instance | nil` that represents the hierarchical parent of the object. It is `nil` when the instance has no parent in the hierarchy. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/instance.md

Instance.Clone() is a method that returns a copy of the Instance as a new `Instance`. It is one of the common methods shared across Instance-like objects in Vortex. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/instance.md

Instance.Destroy() is a method that destroys the Instance along with its children and returns `nil`. It is one of the common methods shared across Instance-like objects in Vortex. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/instance.md

Instance.GetChildren() is a method that returns a table/array `{ Instance }` containing the children of the Instance. It is one of the common methods shared across Instance-like objects in Vortex. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/instance.md

TweenService is a service in Vortex that creates Tween objects used to smoothly interpolate an instance's properties between two states over a period of time. It is obtained via the standard service accessor pattern, such as `game:GetService("TweenService")`. Tweens produced by TweenService are started and controlled through methods on the returned Tween object. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/tween-service.md

TweenService:Create is a method that builds and returns a Tween configured to animate a target instance. It accepts three parameters: an Instance to animate, an optional TweenInfo describing timing/easing, and a goals table that maps property name strings (e.g. `"Position"`, `"Color"`, `"Transparency"`) to their desired target values. Once created, the returned Tween is activated by calling `Tween:Play()`; the goals table does not need to include every property, only those you want interpolated. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/tween-service.md

A Tween is the object returned by TweenService:Create that represents a pending smooth interpolation between an instance's current property values and a set of target values. It is configured with a specific Instance, TweenInfo, and goals table at creation time. To actually run the animation, you call `Tween:Play()` on it. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/tween-service.md

TweenInfo is the configuration object passed to TweenService:Create that describes how a tween's interpolation runs, including its duration and other timing/easing parameters. It is constructed separately (e.g. via `TweenInfo.new(0.1)`) and then supplied as the second argument to TweenService:Create. The method signature accepts TweenInfo as an optional parameter. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/classes/tween-service.md

TweenInfo is a data container that holds configuration parameters describing how a tween should animate, such as duration, easing style, direction, repeat count, reverse behavior, and delay. It is passed into TweenService to define the behavior of a tween animation. All six fields are optional and default to reasonable values if not provided. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/tween-info.md

TweenInfo.new is the constructor that returns a TweenInfo configured with the supplied animation parameters. Its signature is TweenInfo.new(time: Number?, easingStyle: Enum.EasingStyle?, easingDirection: Enum.EasingDirection?, repeatCount: Number?, reverses: Boolean?, delayTime: Number?), and every argument is optional. When omitted, Time defaults to 1, EasingStyle to Quad, EasingDirection to Out, RepeatCount to 0, Reverses to false, and DelayTime to 0. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/tween-info.md

Time is a Number property of TweenInfo that specifies how long the tween takes to run, measured in seconds. It corresponds to the first constructor argument and defaults to 1 when not provided. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/tween-info.md

EasingStyle is an Enum.EasingStyle property of TweenInfo that selects the mathematical easing curve used during interpolation. It defaults to Enum.EasingStyle.Quad when no value is passed to the constructor. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/tween-info.md

EasingDirection is an Enum.EasingDirection property of TweenInfo that determines the direction in which the easing style applies (such as In, Out, or InOut). It defaults to Enum.EasingDirection.Out when not explicitly set. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/tween-info.md

RepeatCount is a Number property of TweenInfo that controls how many additional times the tween plays after the first run. A value of 0 plays once, and -1 means the tween repeats forever. It defaults to 0 when omitted. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/tween-info.md

Reverses is a Boolean property of TweenInfo that, when true, causes the tween to play back to its starting value after reaching its goal, producing a back-and-forth animation. It defaults to false. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/tween-info.md

DelayTime is a Number property of TweenInfo specifying how many seconds the tween should wait before starting. It defaults to 0 when not specified. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/tween-info.md

A Tween in Vortex is an object that smoothly animates properties of an object over time, such as position, size, transparency, or color. Tweens are not created directly but are constructed via TweenService. They expose properties for the target Instance and current PlaybackState, methods to control playback, and a Completed event that fires when the tween finishes. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/tween.md

Tween.Instance is a property of a Tween that holds the object the tween acts upon. It is typed as `Instance` and represents the target whose properties are being animated by the tween. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/tween.md

Tween.PlaybackState is a property of a Tween that reflects the current state of the tween, typed as `Enum.PlaybackState`. Possible values include `Playing` while the tween is active and `Cancelled` if the tween was stopped before completing. Other states are defined on `Enum.PlaybackState`. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/tween.md

Tween:Play() is a method on a Tween that returns `nil` and causes the tween to start playing or to continue if it had been paused. It is the primary way to begin or resume a tween's animation. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/tween.md

Tween:Pause() is a method on a Tween that returns `nil` and pauses the tween at its current position. Calling Tween:Play() again will resume the animation from where it was paused. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/tween.md

Tween:Cancel() is a method on a Tween that returns `nil` and stops the tween at its current position while resetting it to the starting values. Cancellation also causes the Completed event to fire with the Cancelled playback state. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/tween.md

Tween.Completed is an event on a Tween that fires when the tween finishes, whether it completed naturally or was stopped early with Cancel(). The connected callback receives one argument, a `Enum.PlaybackState` value of either `Completed` or `Cancelled`, which lets you determine the reason the tween ended. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/tween.md

Vector3 is a three-dimensional vector type in Vortex representing a position or direction using X, Y, and Z numeric components. It supports common vector operations like dot product, cross product, and linear interpolation, and includes both read-only instance properties and static constants such as zero, one, and the axis unit vectors. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/vector3.md

X is a Number property of a Vector3 representing its component along the X axis. It can be read and assigned like any standard numeric field. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/vector3.md

Y is a Number property of a Vector3 representing its component along the Y axis. It is read and written just like the X component. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/vector3.md

Z is a Number property of a Vector3 representing its component along the Z axis. It completes the three numeric components that define the vector. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/vector3.md

Magnitude is a Number property of a Vector3 that gives the length of the vector (also known as its magnitude). It is computed from the X, Y, and Z components. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/vector3.md

Unit is a Vector3 property of a Vector3 that returns the normalized form of the vector, pointing in the same direction but with a magnitude of 1. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/vector3.md

zero is a static Vector3 constant equal to (0, 0, 0). It is accessed as Vector3.zero and serves as the additive identity for vectors. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/vector3.md
one is a static Vector3 constant equal to (1, 1, 1). It is accessed as Vector3.one. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/vector3.md

xAxis is a static Vector3 constant representing the unit vector along the X axis, with the value (1, 0, 0). It is accessed as Vector3.xAxis. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/vector3.md

yAxis is a static Vector3 constant representing the unit vector along the Y axis, with the value (0, 1, 0). It is accessed as Vector3.yAxis. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/vector3.md

zAxis is a static Vector3 constant representing the unit vector along the Z axis, with the value (0, 0, 1). It is accessed as Vector3.zAxis. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/vector3.md

Vector3.new(X: Number, Y: Number, Z: Number) is the constructor that returns a new Vector3 built from the supplied X, Y, and Z component numbers. All three arguments are required to define the resulting vector. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/vector3.md

Dot(other: Vector3) is a method on Vector3 that returns the dot product of the calling vector and the other vector passed in as a Number. The result is a scalar value derived from the component-wise sum of products. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/vector3.md

Cross(other: Vector3) is a method on Vector3 that returns the cross product of the calling vector and the other vector, producing a Vector3 perpendicular to both inputs. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/vector3.md

Lerp(other: Vector3, alpha: Number) is a method on Vector3 that returns a vector interpolated between self and other. When alpha is 0.0 the result equals self, when alpha is 0.5 the result is the midpoint, and when alpha is 1.0 the result equals other. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/vector3.md

questions: Explain Vector3 Addition Operator in Vortex
How do I use Vector3 Addition Operator?
Tell me about Vector3 Addition Operator
answer: The + operator applied to two Vector3 values returns a Vector3 whose components are the sums of the corresponding X, Y, and Z components of the operands. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/datatypes/vector3.md

questions: Explain Vector3 Subtraction Operator in Vortex

TweenService is a global service in Vortex used to smoothly animate supported properties of an object over a specified duration. It can be accessed either through the global alias `TweenService` or via `game:GetService("TweenService")`. The service lets developers configure how a property changes using easing styles and directions. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/tween-service.md

`TweenService:Create()` constructs a tween instance given a target object, a TweenInfo configuration, and a goal table describing the property values to reach. The created tween does not start automatically; it must be started by calling `:Play()` on the returned object. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/tween-service.md

TweenInfo is a data object built with `TweenInfo.new()` that defines how a tween behaves. Its constructor accepts parameters including the duration in seconds, an `Enum.EasingStyle`, and an `Enum.EasingDirection`. Additional easing styles and directions are documented on the Enum reference page. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/tween-service.md

`TweenInfo.new()` is the constructor used to create a TweenInfo configuration for a tween. Typical arguments include a numeric duration, an easing style from `Enum.EasingStyle` (such as `Linear`), and an easing direction from `Enum.EasingDirection` (such as `Out`). It encapsulates the timing and easing behavior applied to a tween. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/tween-service.md

`Tween:Play()` is the method that starts a tween previously built with `TweenService:Create()`. When invoked, it smoothly applies the configured property changes from the goal table to the target object over the TweenInfo duration and easing. Only properties that support interpolation can be animated this way. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/tween-service.md

UserInputService is a service in the Vortex platform used to detect a player's device and to detect inputs from the player. It is obtained via game:GetService and can only be used in a LocalScript; it is not available in a standard server Script. In Vortex Studio 0.3.4 testing, the client reported KeyboardEnabled=true, MouseEnabled=true, GamepadEnabled=false, and TouchEnabled=false. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/user-input-service.md

IsKeyDown is a method on UserInputService that reports whether a specific key is currently being held down. Its signature is UserInputService:IsKeyDown(KeyCode: Enum.KeyCode): Boolean, taking an Enum.KeyCode and returning a boolean (true while pressed, false otherwise). In Vortex 0.3.4 it is available and works for keyboard keys, but returned false for mouse-button events; mouse buttons arrive with Enum.KeyCode.Unknown. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/user-input-service.md

InputBegan is an event on UserInputService that fires whenever the player begins interacting with an input device. It is connected with signature UserInputService.InputBegan(Input: InputObject, GameProcessedEvent: Boolean), where Input is an InputObject describing the input and GameProcessedEvent is a boolean that is true when the engine already consumed the input (e.g. a UI click). In Vortex 0.3.4, InputBegan:Once and InputBegan:Wait delivered right-mouse button input in a LocalScript, while ordinary InputBegan:Connect delivered keyboard keys (S, A, W, Space) and mouse buttons (with Enum.KeyCode.Unknown), and both processed and unprocessed inputs were observed. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/user-input-service.md

InputEnded is an event on UserInputService that fires whenever the player stops interacting with an input device. It uses the same callback signature as InputBegan: (Input: InputObject, GameProcessedEvent: Boolean), where GameProcessedEvent is true if the engine already acted on the input. In Vortex 0.3.4 it can be connected from a LocalScript and delivered both keyboard and mouse-button releases. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/user-input-service.md

In Vortex, the `workspace` keyword is a reference to the game's root Workspace service, which serves as the top-level container for all physical models, parts, and other Instances that exist within it. It is used to look up specific Instances or quickly gather collections of objects from the perspective of the server or client currently running the code. A notable caveat is that Instances may not yet be available during loading, so code must verify that an Instance exists before trying to access it, or it will throw a runtime error. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/globals/workspace.md

Clone() is a method available on every Instance in Vortex that produces a new instance with the same properties and child hierarchy as the original. The returned object is initially parentless, so the caller typically assigns its Parent (for example, to workspace) to insert it into the game world. Cloning never alters the source instance, and any subsequent changes to either the clone or the original will not be reflected in the other. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/instance/clone.md

Destroy() is an instance method that permanently removes the instance and all of its descendants from the game. After being called, the instance cannot be used through normal operations. As a side effect, the method also disconnects any connections tied to the instance and detaches it from its current parent. Typical usage involves calling it directly on an instance, such as part:Destroy(). Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/instance/destroy.md

FindFirstChild is a method on Instance that searches for a direct child of the instance matching a given name. It takes a single string argument specifying the child name to look for. The method returns the found Instance, or nil if no matching child exists. For example, workspace:FindFirstChild("Part") retrieves a child named "Part" from the workspace, returning nil if none is present. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/instance/findfirstchild.md

GetChildren is an instance method that returns an array of all direct children belonging to the instance on which it is called. The returned value is of type Array. Only first-level descendants are included; objects nested deeper within those children are excluded from the result. A typical usage is calling it on a parent such as workspace, for example local children = workspace:GetChildren(). Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/instance/getchildren.md

WaitForChild is an Instance method that waits for a direct child with a given name to exist and yields the current thread until it appears. It takes a required name parameter of type String and an optional timeout of type Number, and returns an Instance (or nil if the timeout expires). If a matching child already exists, it is returned immediately without yielding; otherwise, the call blocks until the child is added or the specified timeout elapses, in which case nil is returned instead of an instance. Source: https://github.com/TheHaloDeveloper/vortex-docs/blob/main/content/reference/instance/waitforchild.md
